# Command line

<!-- Generated by `chipload reference`; do not edit. Regenerate with CHIPLOAD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p chipload-cli --test guide. -->

Every command takes `--json`: one JSON object instead of text (see [Scripting](../scripting.md)). `chipload --help` and `chipload COMMAND --help` print the same help in the terminal.

## `chipload inspect`

Dump units, entities, contours and issues of a DXF, an SVG or a project

```text
chipload inspect <FILE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FILE>` | A .dxf or .svg drawing or a .chipload project. |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Units of a DXF that does not declare them. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `--px-per-inch <PX_PER_INCH>` | Pixels per inch of an SVG that gives no real size: 96 (Inkscape, browsers) or 72 (older Illustrator) |

## `chipload new`

Create an empty project, to draw in or import a DXF into later (`update --from`)

```text
chipload new [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | The project to write (.chipload) Required. |
| `--machine <MACHINE>` | The machine profile to start from (default: your default machine) |

## `chipload import`

Create a project from a DXF or an SVG

```text
chipload import <DXF> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<DXF>` | The DXF or SVG (.svg, .svgz) |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Units of a DXF that does not declare them. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `--px-per-inch <PX_PER_INCH>` | Pixels per inch of an SVG that gives no real size: 96 (Inkscape, browsers) or 72 (older Illustrator) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | The project to write (.chipload) Required. |
| `--machine <MACHINE>` | The machine profile to start from (default: your default machine) |

## `chipload update`

Replace a project's imported drawing with a new version of the DXF or SVG

```text
chipload update <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--from <FROM>` | The new DXF or SVG. Required. |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Units of the new DXF, if they differ from the last import. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `--px-per-inch <PX_PER_INCH>` | Pixels per inch of an SVG without a real size, if they differ from the last import. |
| `--dxf <DXF>` | Which DXF of the project (as `dxf list` shows); needed when it has several. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload plan`

Plan a project's toolpath without writing G-code

```text
chipload plan <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--setup <ID>` | Only this setup (as `setup list` numbers it); default: every setup for `run`, the active one otherwise (docs/specs/setups.md §8) |
| `--part <ID>` | Only this part (as `part list` numbers it), as if every other part were switched off; may be given more than once (docs/specs/part-export.md) Repeatable. |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload run`

Generate checked G-code from a project

```text
chipload run <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the G-code. With several tools and one file per tool: part.nc gives part-1-T1.nc, part-2-T2.nc, ... Required. |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | For this run only: one file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes (default: the project's machine setting) One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |
| `--no-sheet` | Don't write the setup sheet (by default `part-sheet.html` next to `part.nc`) |
| `--sheet-units <UNITS>` | The setup sheet's lengths and feeds: mm (default) or inch. The G-code's units are the machine's (machine.gcode_units) One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `--sheet-lang <LANG>` | The setup sheet's language (default: English). The command line itself stays English. One of: `en`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `it`, `sv`. |
| `--setup <ID>` | Only this setup (as `setup list` numbers it); default: every setup for `run`, the active one otherwise (docs/specs/setups.md §8) |
| `--part <ID>` | Only this part (as `part list` numbers it), as if every other part were switched off; may be given more than once (docs/specs/part-export.md) Repeatable. |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload simulate`

Simulate the material a project's program removes (docs/specs/simulation.md): print the numbers and write a shaded top view (PNG). The job is generated and checked as by `run`; no G-code is written

```text
chipload simulate <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the image (.png); default: the project's name with `-sim.png`. |
| `--cell <CELL>` | Cell size, mm (default: automatic, from the stock's size) |
| `--no-image` | Print the numbers only. |
| `--after <N>` | The stock after only the first N moves of the program (docs/specs/playback.md §5), for tests and scripts. |
| `--setup <ID>` | The setup to simulate (as `setup list` numbers it); default: the active one. |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload sheet`

Write a project's setup sheet for the operator (HTML), without the G-code. The job is generated and checked as by `run`

```text
chipload sheet <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the sheet (.html) Required. |
| `--gcode <GCODE>` | The G-code the sheet is for, as given to `run -o`, for its file names (default: the project's name with the post's extension) |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | For this sheet only: one file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes. One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |
| `--units <UNITS>` | Its lengths and feeds: mm (default) or inch. The G-code's units are the machine's (machine.gcode_units) One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `--lang <LANG>` | Its language (default: English). The command line itself stays English. One of: `en`, `de`, `fr`, `es`, `it`, `sv`. |
| `--setup <ID>` | Only this setup (as `setup list` numbers it); default: every setup for `run`, the active one otherwise (docs/specs/setups.md §8) |
| `--part <ID>` | Only this part (as `part list` numbers it), as if every other part were switched off; may be given more than once (docs/specs/part-export.md) Repeatable. |
| `--set <PATH=VALUE>` | For this run only: set a project value by path, e.g. `stock.thickness=18` (see `chipload set`). The project file isn't changed. Repeatable. |

## `chipload render`

Render a toolpath JSON (as `plan --json` prints under "program") through a post-processor. For testing posts; the output is NOT checked, use `run` to cut

```text
chipload render <PROGRAM> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROGRAM>` | Toolpath JSON file. |
| `--post <POST>` | Built-in post-processor. Default: `grbl`. |

## `chipload check`

Check a G-code program against a project's stock, safe height and machine limits

```text
chipload check <GCODE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<GCODE>` | G-code file to check. |
| `--job <JOB>` | The project (or job) the program was generated from. Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The project's tool that cuts this program, for its stock margin (one file of a set written one file per tool). Default: the largest tool the project uses. |

## `chipload op`

Change an operation of a project

### `chipload op tool`

Set the tool an operation cuts with (docs/specs/tool-per-operation.md §7). The tool must be in the project: copy one in from your library with `tool use`

```text
chipload op tool <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation's number as the app lists it (1 = first; `get` and `set` paths count from 0) Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The tool's id in the project. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op add-rest`

Add a rest pass to a pocket (docs/specs/rest-passes.md): a smaller endmill that clears what the pocket's tool (or its last pass's) leaves, in the pocket's shapes and depths. It is cut after the run of pockets with the pocket's tool

```text
chipload op add-rest <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The pocket's number as the app lists it (1 = first; `get` and `set` paths count from 0) Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The smaller tool's id in the project. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op add-floor`

Give a V-carve a floor pass (docs/specs/vcarve-wide-strokes.md §4): an end mill that clears the floor between the walls of strokes too wide to carve from their centre line, cut before the V-carve. Replaces the floor pass it had

```text
chipload op add-floor <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The V-carve's number as the app lists it (1 = first; `get` and `set` paths count from 0) Required. |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The end mill's id in the project. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op remove-floor`

Take a V-carve's floor pass away (docs/specs/vcarve-wide-strokes.md §4)

```text
chipload op remove-floor <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The V-carve's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op add-surface`

Add a surface (docs/specs/surfacing.md): the whole stock taken down flat with a wide endmill, in straight passes back and forth, first in the active part. Flattens the spoilboard or faces the stock

```text
chipload op add-surface <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The endmill's id in the project; default: the widest endmill. |
| `--depth <DEPTH>` | How much comes off the top; default 0.5 mm. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op rest-pass`

A pocket's rest passes (docs/specs/rest-passes.md): without --pass, list them; with it, change, turn off or on, or remove one

```text
chipload op rest-pass <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The pocket's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |
| `--pass <PASS>` | Which pass: 1 for the first (shown as 3.1 for operation 3) |
| `--tool <TOOL>` | The tool's id in the project: an endmill smaller than the tool before it. |
| `--feed <FEED>` |  |
| `--plunge-feed <PLUNGE_FEED>` |  |
| `--step-down <STEP_DOWN>` |  |
| `--stepover <STEPOVER>` | A fraction of the tool's diameter, at most 1. |
| `--enabled <ENABLED>` | Cut it (true) or keep it without cutting (false) One of: `true`, `false`. |
| `--remove` | Remove the pass; the passes after it rest after the tool before it. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op make-rest-pass`

Make a rest pocket that copies an earlier pocket (same shapes, depths, clearance and direction, rest after its tool) a rest pass of that pocket (docs/specs/rest-passes.md §5). It is then cut after the run of pockets it belongs to

```text
chipload op make-rest-pass <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The rest pocket's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op part`

Move an operation into another part, at the end of its operations (docs/specs/parts.md §7). Operations are numbered again in the new order

```text
chipload op part <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation's number as the app lists it (1 = first; `get` and `set` paths count from 0) Required. |
| `--part <PART>` | The part's id (as `part list` shows it) Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op corners`

List a profile's or pocket's corners on the tool's side, with what each gets (round, dogbone, T-bone along the longer or shorter wall) and whether that is the corner's own choice (docs/specs/dogbone-per-corner.md)

```text
chipload op corners <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |

### `chipload op corner`

Give one corner of a profile or pocket its own bone, whatever the operation's corners say (docs/specs/dogbone-per-corner.md): `--bone none` keeps it round. `op corners` lists the corners

```text
chipload op corner <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |
| `--at <AT>` | The corner, X,Y in drawing coordinates (a plain number is mm) |
| `--bone <BONE>` | What the corner gets. One of: `none`, `dogbone`, `tbone`. |
| `--along <ALONG>` | With a T-bone: the wall it runs along (the notch is in the other); default longer. One of: `longer`, `shorter`. |
| `--as-operation` | Remove the corner's own choice: it gets what the operation gives every corner. |
| `--reset` | Remove every corner's own choice. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op tabs`

List a profile's tabs: each contour's, with their centres on the tool path and whether they were placed by hand (docs/specs/tabs-by-hand.md). The job is planned

```text
chipload op tabs <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |

### `chipload op tab`

Place a profile's tabs by hand (docs/specs/tabs-by-hand.md): add a tab at a point, or remove the one there. The first on a contour keeps that contour's other tabs where Chipload put them. `--even` spaces one contour's tabs evenly again, `--reset` all

```text
chipload op tab <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The operation's number as the app lists it (1 = first) Required. |
| `--at <AT>` | The point, X,Y in drawing coordinates (a plain number is mm): on or near the contour, within a tool diameter. |
| `--remove` | Remove the tab nearest to --at. |
| `--even` | Space the tabs of the contour nearest to --at evenly again. |
| `--reset` | Space every contour's tabs evenly again. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload op rest`

Make a pocket clear only what a larger tool leaves (docs/specs/rest-machining.md)

```text
chipload op rest <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--op <OP>` | The pocket's number as the app lists it (1 = first; `get` and `set` paths count from 0) Required. |
| `--after-tool <AFTER_TOOL>` | The larger tool's id in the project. |
| `--none` | Clear the whole pocket again. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload shape`

Draw in a project: add, change or delete circles, rectangles and polylines

### `chipload shape add`

Add a drawn shape; prints its id

```text
chipload shape add <PROJECT> <KIND> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<KIND>` | One of: `circle`, `rectangle`, `polyline`, `polygon`. |
| `--center <CENTER>` | Centre "X,Y" (circle, rectangle, polygon) |
| `--radius <RADIUS>` | A circle's radius; a polygon's, to its corners. |
| `--sides <SIDES>` | A polygon's number of sides, 3 to 1000. |
| `--across-flats <ACROSS_FLATS>` | A polygon's size across its flats (twice the radius to the middle of a side), in place of --radius. |
| `--length <LENGTH>` | Along the rectangle's own X axis. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Along the rectangle's own Y axis. |
| `--angle-deg <ANGLE_DEG>` | Rotation about the centre (a polygon: its first corner's angle from +X), degrees, counter-clockwise. |
| `--corner-radius <CORNER_RADIUS>` | The radius of the rectangle's corners, at most half its shorter side (default 0: sharp) |
| `--points <POINTS>` | Polyline points "X,Y X,Y ...". |
| `--bulges <BULGES>` | Polyline bulges "B B ...", one per segment: tan(sweep / 4) as in DXF, 0 straight, 1 a counter-clockwise half circle, -1 clockwise (default: all straight) |
| `--open` | The polyline doesn't return to its first point. |
| `--closed` | The polyline returns to its first point (the default for new ones) |
| `--layer <LAYER>` |  |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its name in the Browser; "" takes the name away. |
| `--construction <CONSTRUCTION>` | Construction geometry: shown and snapped to, never cut (`--construction false` makes it an ordinary shape again) One of: `true`, `false`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape set`

Change a drawn shape's values or layer; it keeps its id

```text
chipload shape set <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--center <CENTER>` | Centre "X,Y" (circle, rectangle, polygon) |
| `--radius <RADIUS>` | A circle's radius; a polygon's, to its corners. |
| `--sides <SIDES>` | A polygon's number of sides, 3 to 1000. |
| `--across-flats <ACROSS_FLATS>` | A polygon's size across its flats (twice the radius to the middle of a side), in place of --radius. |
| `--length <LENGTH>` | Along the rectangle's own X axis. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Along the rectangle's own Y axis. |
| `--angle-deg <ANGLE_DEG>` | Rotation about the centre (a polygon: its first corner's angle from +X), degrees, counter-clockwise. |
| `--corner-radius <CORNER_RADIUS>` | The radius of the rectangle's corners, at most half its shorter side (default 0: sharp) |
| `--points <POINTS>` | Polyline points "X,Y X,Y ...". |
| `--bulges <BULGES>` | Polyline bulges "B B ...", one per segment: tan(sweep / 4) as in DXF, 0 straight, 1 a counter-clockwise half circle, -1 clockwise (default: all straight) |
| `--open` | The polyline doesn't return to its first point. |
| `--closed` | The polyline returns to its first point (the default for new ones) |
| `--layer <LAYER>` |  |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its name in the Browser; "" takes the name away. |
| `--construction <CONSTRUCTION>` | Construction geometry: shown and snapped to, never cut (`--construction false` makes it an ordinary shape again) One of: `true`, `false`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape remove`

Remove a drawn shape. Operations that used it are flagged

```text
chipload shape remove <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` |  |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape copy`

Copy drawn shapes, moved by --dx and --dy, on their layers; prints the new ids

```text
chipload shape copy <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--dx <DX>` | How far to move the copies right, mm. Required. |
| `--dy <DY>` | How far to move the copies up, mm. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape mirror`

Mirror drawn shapes in place, about the middle of the box round them. They keep their ids, so the operations that cut them follow

```text
chipload shape mirror <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--axis <AXIS>` | x: flip the X coordinates (left becomes right); y: flip Y (up becomes down) One of: `x`, `y`. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape move`

Move drawn shapes by --dx and --dy; they keep their ids, so the operations that cut them follow (docs/specs/drawn-shapes-box.md)

```text
chipload shape move <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--dx <DX>` | How far to move them right, mm. Required. |
| `--dy <DY>` | How far to move them up, mm. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape turn`

Turn drawn shapes counter-clockwise about the middle of the box round them, or a point

```text
chipload shape turn <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--angle-deg <ANGLE_DEG>` | The angle, degrees, counter-clockwise; negative turns clockwise. Required. |
| `--about <ABOUT>` | Turn about this point "X,Y" instead. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape scale`

Scale drawn shapes evenly about the middle of the box round them, or a point

```text
chipload shape scale <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--factor <FACTOR>` | The factor, greater than 0: 2 doubles them. Required. |
| `--about <ABOUT>` | Scale about this point "X,Y" instead. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape offset`

Add the curve at a distance from drawn shapes, on their layers; the shapes stay (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §2). Prints the new ids

```text
chipload shape offset <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--distance <DISTANCE>` | How far, mm (or with a unit) Required. |
| `--side <SIDE>` | Which side: outside or inside of a closed shape, left or right of an open one (default: outside, or left) One of: `outside`, `inside`, `left`, `right`. |
| `--corners <CORNERS>` | Round corners (the exact offset) or sharp ones (the sides extended to meet) One of: `round`, `sharp`. Default: `round`. |
| `--count <COUNT>` | How many, each the distance further than the last. Default: `1`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape fillet`

Round corners of a drawn shape with arcs of a radius; it keeps its id (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §3)

```text
chipload shape fillet <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--radius <RADIUS>` | The radius, mm (or with a unit) Required. |
| `--corner <CORNER>` | Only this corner: its point's number, from 0 (default: every corner) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape trim`

Trim a drawn shape: the piece of it at --at, between the nearest crossings with the shapes shown, goes; the rest keeps the id, a second piece is a new shape (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §4)

```text
chipload shape trim <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--at <AT>` | A point on (or near) the piece to remove, "X,Y". Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape extend`

Extend an open drawn shape's straight end along itself to the nearest shape shown ahead (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §4)

```text
chipload shape extend <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--end <END>` | Which end. One of: `start`, `end`. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape break`

Break a drawn shape at the point of it nearest --at: an open one becomes two, a closed one opens there (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §4)

```text
chipload shape break <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--at <AT>` | The point, "X,Y". Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape union`

Join closed drawn shapes into one: everything any of them covers. The result takes the first shape's id; the others go (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §5)

```text
chipload shape union <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids, two or more (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape subtract`

Cut closed drawn shapes out of another: BASE keeps its id, the cutters go (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §5)

```text
chipload shape subtract <PROJECT> <BASE> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<BASE>` | The shape cut (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `<IDS>` | The shapes cut out of it. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape intersect`

What closed drawn shapes have in common: the result takes the first shape's id; the others go (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §5)

```text
chipload shape intersect <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids, two or more (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape array`

Copies of drawn shapes in a grid, on their layers; the originals stay (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §6). Prints the new ids

```text
chipload shape array <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--columns <COLUMNS>` | Columns, the originals' included. Default: `1`. |
| `--rows <ROWS>` | Rows, the originals' included. Default: `1`. |
| `--dx <DX>` | From one column to the next, mm (or with a unit); negative goes left. Default: `0`. |
| `--dy <DY>` | From one row to the next, mm (or with a unit); negative goes down. Default: `0`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape array-polar`

Copies of drawn shapes round a centre, on their layers; the originals stay (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §6). Prints the new ids

```text
chipload shape array-polar <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--count <COUNT>` | How many, the originals included. Required. |
| `--center <CENTER>` | The centre, "X,Y". Required. |
| `--angle-deg <ANGLE_DEG>` | The sweep, degrees: 360 spreads them evenly round, less puts the first and last at its ends; negative goes clockwise. Default: `360`. |
| `--no-rotate` | Move the copies round without turning them. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape align`

Line up drawn shapes: each one's box side or middle with that of the box round them all, or the stock's; they move whole and keep their ids (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §7)

```text
chipload shape align <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--to <TO>` | Which side or middle lines up. One of: `left`, `centre`, `right`, `top`, `middle`, `bottom`. Required. |
| `--stock` | Line up with the stock instead (then one shape is enough) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape distribute`

Even out the gaps between drawn shapes' boxes, the first and last staying put (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §7)

```text
chipload shape distribute <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids, three or more (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) |
| `--horizontal` | Along X. |
| `--vertical` | Along Y. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape chamfer`

Cut corners of a drawn shape straight across, a distance back along each side; it keeps its id (docs/specs/drawing-editing.md §3)

```text
chipload shape chamfer <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The shape id (as `inspect` lists it, without the S) |
| `--distance <DISTANCE>` | How far back along each side, mm (or with a unit) Required. |
| `--corner <CORNER>` | Only this corner: its point's number, from 0 (default: every corner) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload shape join`

Join open drawn polylines whose ends are closer than --gap into one, on the same layer; a chain that comes back to its start closes (docs/specs/explode-and-join.md)

```text
chipload shape join <PROJECT> <IDS>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<IDS>` | The shape ids (as `inspect` lists them, without the S); none: every drawn shape. |
| `--gap <GAP>` | Join ends closer than this, 0.001 to 1 mm. Default: `0.01`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload image`

Pictures traced into shapes for V-carving: add, change, list, preview, remove

### `chipload image add`

Add a picture (PNG, JPEG or BMP) and trace it into shapes on its own layer

```text
chipload image add <PROJECT> <PICTURE> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<PICTURE>` | The picture. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | The picture's width on the stock, mm; its height follows. Required. |
| `--layer <LAYER>` | The layer for its shapes; default: the picture's file name. |
| `--invert` | Carve the light parts instead of the dark ones. |
| `--at <AT>` | Where the picture's lower-left corner goes: X,Y in mm (default 0,0) |
| `--threshold <THRESHOLD>` | Grey values (0–255) below this are black: 1 to 254, or auto (default) |
| `--blur <BLUR>` | Blur before the threshold, px, 0 to 10 (default 1) |
| `--min-area <MIN_AREA>` | Drop specks smaller than this, mm², 0 to 100 (default 0.5) |
| `--smoothing <SMOOTHING>` | How far an edge may be simplified, mm, 0.01 to 1 (default 0.05) |
| `--trace <TRACE>` | What to trace: outline (for a V-carve, default) or centre-line (strokes, for a follow path) |
| `--arcs <ARCS>` | Fit arcs as well as lines (true or false; default true) One of: `true`, `false`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload image set`

Change an image's settings, position or size, and trace it again

```text
chipload image set <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The image's id (as `image list` shows it) |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | The picture's width on the stock, mm. |
| `--rotate <ROTATE>` | Turn it about its centre to this angle, degrees counter-clockwise (any angle; 0: as the picture is). `--at` stays the corner before the turn. |
| `--layer <LAYER>` | The layer for its shapes. |
| `--invert <INVERT>` | Carve the light parts instead (true or false) One of: `true`, `false`. |
| `--at <AT>` | Where the picture's lower-left corner goes: X,Y in mm (default 0,0) |
| `--threshold <THRESHOLD>` | Grey values (0–255) below this are black: 1 to 254, or auto (default) |
| `--blur <BLUR>` | Blur before the threshold, px, 0 to 10 (default 1) |
| `--min-area <MIN_AREA>` | Drop specks smaller than this, mm², 0 to 100 (default 0.5) |
| `--smoothing <SMOOTHING>` | How far an edge may be simplified, mm, 0.01 to 1 (default 0.05) |
| `--trace <TRACE>` | What to trace: outline (for a V-carve, default) or centre-line (strokes, for a follow path) |
| `--arcs <ARCS>` | Fit arcs as well as lines (true or false; default true) One of: `true`, `false`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload image list`

The project's images: picture, place, settings and shapes

```text
chipload image list <PROJECT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

Write an image as black and white, as it is traced (PNG)

```text
chipload image preview <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | The PNG to write. Required. |

Remove an image and its shapes

## `chipload text`

Text written into shapes for V-carving, pocketing or profiling: add, change, list, remove, and the built-in fonts (docs/specs/text.md)

### `chipload text add`

Write a text into shapes on its own layer; prints its id. "\n" in the text starts a new line

```text
chipload text add <PROJECT> <TEXT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<TEXT>` | What it says. |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | The height of a capital letter, mm. Required. |
| `--at <AT>` | Where the text's anchor goes: X,Y in mm (default 0,0) |
| `--anchor <ANCHOR>` | What --at is: the lower-left corner of the text's box (default) or its centre. A centred text stays centred when it changes. Changed without --at, the text stays where it is. One of: `corner`, `center`. |
| `--rotate <ROTATE>` | Turn it about its centre to this angle, degrees counter-clockwise (any angle). `--at` stays the corner before the turn. |
| `--font <FONT>` | A built-in font (`text fonts`; default FreeSans) |
| `--align <ALIGN>` | How the lines line up (default left) One of: `left`, `center`, `right`. |
| `--spacing <SPACING>` | Extra space between letters, mm (default 0: the font's own) |
| `--line-spacing <LINE_SPACING>` | From one line's base to the next, in capital heights (default 1.6) |
| `--layer <LAYER>` | The layer for its letters (default "text") |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload text set`

Change a text (what it says, its font, size, place or turn) and write it again

```text
chipload text set <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

| `--text <TEXT>` | What it says. |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | The height of a capital letter, mm. |
| `--at <AT>` | Where the text's anchor goes: X,Y in mm (default 0,0) |
| `--anchor <ANCHOR>` | What --at is: the lower-left corner of the text's box (default) or its centre. A centred text stays centred when it changes. Changed without --at, the text stays where it is. One of: `corner`, `center`. |
| `--rotate <ROTATE>` | Turn it about its centre to this angle, degrees counter-clockwise (any angle). `--at` stays the corner before the turn. |
| `--font <FONT>` | A built-in font (`text fonts`; default FreeSans) |
| `--align <ALIGN>` | How the lines line up (default left) One of: `left`, `center`, `right`. |
| `--spacing <SPACING>` | Extra space between letters, mm (default 0: the font's own) |
| `--line-spacing <LINE_SPACING>` | From one line's base to the next, in capital heights (default 1.6) |
| `--layer <LAYER>` | The layer for its letters (default "text") |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload dxf`

A project's DXFs: add another, list them, remove one (docs/specs/drawing-sources.md)

### `chipload dxf add`

Add a DXF or an SVG to the project, where the file has it; move it with `place --dxf ID` (an SVG shares the DXFs' numbers and commands)

```text
chipload dxf add <PROJECT> <DXF> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<DXF>` | The DXF or SVG (.svg, .svgz) |
| `--units <UNITS>` | The DXF's units, if it doesn't say. |
| `--px-per-inch <PX_PER_INCH>` | An SVG's pixels per inch, if it gives no real size: 96 (Inkscape, browsers) or 72 (older Illustrator) |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its name; default: the file's name without its extension. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload dxf list`

The project's DXFs: id, name, file, placement and shapes

```text
chipload dxf list <PROJECT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

### `chipload dxf explode`

Turn a DXF's shapes into drawn shapes you can edit; the project no longer knows the DXF (docs/specs/explode-and-join.md). Operations keep cutting the same shapes

```text
chipload dxf explode <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The DXF's id (as `dxf list` shows it); not needed when the project has one. |
| `--join <JOIN>` | Then join ends closer than this (as `shape join --gap`), e.g. 0.01 or 0.05mm. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload dxf export`

Write the drawing as a DXF: every shape the canvas shows, where it shows it, on its layers, in mm (docs/specs/dxf-export.md). The file is read back before it is written

```text
chipload dxf export <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | The DXF to write. Required. |
| `--inch` | In inches instead of mm. |
| `--hidden` | Hidden groups and layers too. |
| `--layer <LAYERS>` | Only this layer (repeat for more) Repeatable. |
| `--shape <SHAPES>` | Only these shapes, by id (as `inspect` lists them, without the S) Repeatable. |
| `--construction` | Construction geometry too, each on a layer of its own (LAYER_construction) |

### `chipload dxf remove`

Remove a DXF and its shapes

```text
chipload dxf remove <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The DXF's id (as `dxf list` shows it) |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload machine list`

List the machine profiles and where they are kept

```text
chipload machine list
```

### `chipload machine add`

Add a machine profile. Values not given are the built-in project defaults

```text
chipload machine add <NAME> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |
| `--post <POST>` | Built-in post-processor. |
| `--safe-z <SAFE_Z>` |  |
| `--spindle <SPINDLE>` | One of: `cw`, `ccw`. |
| `--max-feed <MAX_FEED>` |  |
| `--travel <TRAVEL>` | Travel "X,Y,Z". |
| `--work-zero <WORK_ZERO>` | drawing-origin, stock-center, stock-bottom-left, stock-bottom-right, stock-top-left, stock-top-right, or a point "X,Y". |
| `--max-overcut <MAX_OVERCUT>` | How far below the stock a cut may go (into the spoilboard) |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | With several tools: one G-code file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes that your sender handles. One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |
| `--gcode-units <GCODE_UNITS>` | The units the G-code is written in: mm (G21) or inch (G20). Everything else stays in mm. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |

### `chipload machine set`

Change a machine profile

```text
chipload machine set <NAME> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<NAME>` |  |
| `--post <POST>` | Built-in post-processor. |
| `--safe-z <SAFE_Z>` |  |
| `--spindle <SPINDLE>` | One of: `cw`, `ccw`. |
| `--max-feed <MAX_FEED>` |  |
| `--travel <TRAVEL>` | Travel "X,Y,Z". |
| `--work-zero <WORK_ZERO>` | drawing-origin, stock-center, stock-bottom-left, stock-bottom-right, stock-top-left, stock-top-right, or a point "X,Y". |
| `--max-overcut <MAX_OVERCUT>` | How far below the stock a cut may go (into the spoilboard) |
| `--tool-change <TOOL_CHANGE>` | With several tools: one G-code file per tool, or one file with M6 tool changes that your sender handles. One of: `files` (One G-code file per tool group), `program` (One file with `T<n> M6` at each tool change). |
| `--gcode-units <GCODE_UNITS>` | The units the G-code is written in: mm (G21) or inch (G20). Everything else stays in mm. One of: `mm`, `inch`. |
| `--rename <RENAME>` | A new name. |

## `chipload post`

Post-processors: the built-in ones and yours (docs/specs/user-posts.md)

### `chipload post list`

List the built-in post-processors and yours, and where yours go

```text
chipload post list
```

### `chipload post show`

What a post-processor writes: its name, files, extension, decimals, arcs, tool change modes and spindle dwell

```text
chipload post show <NAME>
```

|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | The post's name (`chipload post list`) |

### `chipload post use`

Make a post-processor the project's; one of yours is copied into the project (run again after changing it, to update the copy)


| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--post <POST>` | The post's name (`chipload post list`) Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload part`

A project's parts: groups of operations, each cut with its copies before the next (docs/specs/parts.md)

### `chipload part list`

The project's parts: id, name, on or off, copies and operations

```text
chipload part list <PROJECT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

### `chipload part add`

Add an empty part at the end; it becomes the active part

```text
chipload part add <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its name; default: "Part N". |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload part set`

Rename a part, or turn it off or on (a part that is off isn't cut)

```text
chipload part set <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The part's id (as `part list` shows it) |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its new name. |
| `--off` | Leave the part and its operations out of the program. |
| `--on` | Cut the part again. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload part activate`

Make a part the active one: where the app adds new operations

```text
chipload part activate <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The part's id. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload part remove`

Remove a part. Refused while it has operations, unless --with-operations

```text
chipload part remove <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The part's id. |
| `--with-operations` | Remove its operations with it. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload setup`

A project's setups: each a board clamped once, with its stock, work zero and parts, run as a program of its own (docs/specs/setups.md)

### `chipload setup list`

The project's setups: id, name, on or off, board, work zero and parts

```text
chipload setup list <PROJECT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

### `chipload setup add`

Add a setup at the end, a board like the active one's, with a first part of its own; both become active

```text
chipload setup add <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its name; default: "Setup N". |
| `--thickness <THICKNESS>` | Its board's thickness; default: the active setup's. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload setup set`

Rename a setup, or turn it off or on (a setup that is off isn't cut)

```text
chipload setup set <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The setup's id (as `setup list` shows it) |
| `--name <NAME>` | Its new name. |
| `--off` | Leave the setup and its parts out. |
| `--on` | Cut the setup again. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload setup activate`

Make a setup the active one: shown, simulated, where new parts go

```text
chipload setup activate <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The setup's id. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload setup part`

Move a part into a setup: it is cut from that board, with its zero

```text
chipload setup part <PROJECT> <PART> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<PART>` | The part's id (as `part list` shows it) |
| `--to <TO>` | The setup's id. Required. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

### `chipload setup remove`

Remove a setup. Refused while it has parts, unless --with-parts

```text
chipload setup remove <PROJECT> <ID> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<ID>` | The setup's id. |
| `--with-parts` | Remove its parts and their operations with it. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload zero`

Where the G-code's X0 Y0 Z0 is (docs/specs/work-zero-marker.md §5): a corner or the centre of the stock, the drawing origin, or a point. Moving it moves no cut, only the program's numbers. Without an option, print where it is

```text
chipload zero <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--stock <STOCK>` | At a corner or the centre of the stock; it follows the stock's size. One of: `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, `top-left`, `top-right`, `center`. |
| `--drawing-origin` | At the drawing's origin. |
| `--at <AT>` | At the point "X,Y" in drawing coordinates (any length unit; plain numbers are mm) |
| `--z <Z>` | Z0 at the stock's top or bottom. One of: `top`, `bottom`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload copies`

Cut a part several times in a grid (docs/specs/copies-grid.md)

```text
chipload copies <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--part <PART>` | Which part (as `part list` shows it); needed when the project has several. |
| `--grid <GRID>` | Columns x rows, e.g. "3x2". |
| `--pitch <PITCH>` | Pitch "DX,DY" in mm, copy to copy; negative grows left or down. |
| `--gap <GAP>` | Set the pitch so that this many mm are left between the cuts of neighbours. |
| `--order <ORDER>` | The cut order. One of: `by-operation` (Each operation on every copy, then the next operation), `by-copy` (Every operation on one copy, then the next copy (was `by-part`)). |
| `--off` | Back to one copy. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload place`

Move, turn or scale the imported drawing (docs/specs/drawing-placement.md, drawing-rotation.md, drawing-scale.md). Without an option, print where it is

```text
chipload place <PROJECT> [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `--by <BY>` | Move by "DX,DY" mm. |
| `--to <TO>` | Put it "DX,DY" mm from where the DXF has it; 0,0 is as drawn. |
| `--at <AT>` | Put the lower-left corner of its bounding box at "X,Y" mm (the app's Position) |
| `--align <ALIGN>` | Align the drawing's extent with the stock. One of: `bottom-left` (Bottom-left corner on the stock's, --margin mm in), `center` (Centre on the stock's centre). |
| `--margin <MARGIN>` | With --align bottom-left: how far in from the stock's corner, mm. |
| `--rotate <ROTATE>` | Turn it about its centre by this many degrees counter-clockwise (negative: clockwise), any angle, on top of any turn it has. Before --align when both are given. |
| `--scale <SCALE>` | Scale it about its centre by this factor (> 0), on top of any scale it has. After --rotate, before --align. |
| `--width <WIDTH>` | Scale it about its centre until it is this wide, mm (the height follows) |
| `--height <HEIGHT>` | Scale it about its centre until it is this high, mm (the width follows) |
| `--reset` | Back to where the DXF has it: no turn, no scale, no move. |
| `--dxf <DXF>` | Which DXF of the project (as `dxf list` shows); needed when it has several. |
| `--image <IMAGE>` | A picture of the project instead (as `image list` shows it): --at, --rotate and --width apply, as `image set`. |
| `--text <TEXT>` | A text of the project instead (as `text list` shows it): --at (its anchor: the corner or the centre, as set), --rotate and --height (its capital height) apply, as `text set`. |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload set`

Set project values by path (docs/specs/scripting.md §4): `operations.1.end_depth=6.5`. A value is JSON when it parses (6.5, true, null, {"after_tool": 1}), else text. The project must still load; problems are listed but don't stop the write

```text
chipload set <PROJECT> <VALUES>... [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |
| `<VALUES>` |  |
| `-o, --output <OUTPUT>` | Where to write the result; default: the project itself. |

## `chipload check-project`

List a project's problems with their paths, without planning; exits 1 if any

```text
chipload check-project <PROJECT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PROJECT>` | The project (.chipload) |

## `chipload schema`

Print the JSON Schema of a file format (docs/specs/scripting.md §2)

```text
chipload schema <FORMAT>
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<FORMAT>` | One of: `project` (A project file (.chipload)), `tools` (The tool library (tools.json, and `tool export` files)), `machines` (The machine profiles (machines.json, and `machine export` files)), `materials` (The materials (materials.json, and `material export` files)). |

## `chipload mcp`

Serve the commands as tools to an AI assistant over the Model Context Protocol, on stdin and stdout (e.g. `claude mcp add chipload -- chipload mcp`)

```text
chipload mcp
```
